entries.clue: Little attempt to restrict second government department (8)

indicatorNotes.to restrict: to restrict is to hold in, so MINI + TRY holds S between them

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second

annotation.surface: A small effort to curb a second Whitehall ministry.
annotation.walkthrough: "Little attempt" reads as one unit that does the restricting, so the S is caught at the join of its two halves.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: in Britain the big government departments are called ministries, as in the Ministry of Defence.

entries.clue: Left wing group has little time to take on males heading corporation (8)

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a little time
corporation is old slang for a pot belly

indicatorNotes.to take on: to take something on is to add it, so MEN is added after MO
indicatorNotes.heading: to head something is to go in front of it, so MEN comes before TUM

annotation.surface: A left-wing faction takes on extra men at the top of a company.
annotation.walkthrough: Momentum is the left-wing campaign group within the UK Labour Party. "Corporation" looks like a company but is humorous slang for a paunch.
annotation.definitionFit: Momentum is the name of a left-wing Labour pressure group.

entries.clue: (& 29ac.) Condition added to butter by overprotective government (5)

indicatorNotes.added to: one piece is added after the other

blocks.note: a nanny goat butts, so is a butter

annotation.surface: Some rule about butter imposed by a meddling government.
annotation.walkthrough: "Butter" is not the spread but something that butts: a goat. The condition is added after it, so it reads second.
annotation.definitionFit: The nanny state is a government seen as fussily overprotective of its citizens.

entries.clue: Supposedly like Starmer's party, it's pathetic! (9)

indicatorNotes.pathetic: something pathetic is in a sorry state, so the letters of IT'S are left in disarray

blocks.note: a social is an informal party

annotation.surface: A jibe that Starmer's Labour, supposedly left-wing, is feeble.
annotation.walkthrough: "Starmer's party" reads as one phrase meaning Labour, but the definition stops at "Starmer's" and party is a social. Keir Starmer leads the UK Labour Party.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Labour officially calls itself democratic socialist, and "supposedly" is the setter's doubt.

entries.clue: Chancellor's first real cock-up: restricting child reduction (6)

indicatorNotes.cock-up: a cock-up is a mess, so the letters of REAL are messed up
indicatorNotes.restricting: the jumbled letters hold CH inside them
indicatorNotes.reduction: child is reduced to its abbreviation CH

blocks.note: first part of the jumbled REAL
ch is the abbreviation for child

annotation.surface: The Chancellor's first real blunder: cutting child benefit.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the Chancellor's first name: Rachel Reeves became UK Chancellor of the Exchequer in 2024. The rest reads as a news headline.
annotation.definitionFit: Rachel is the first name of Chancellor Rachel Reeves.

entries.clue: Chief, Cyclops is linked to drugs rings! (6)

indicatorNotes.is linked to: the pieces are joined one after another

blocks.note: ch is the abbreviation for chief
Cyclops, the setter, speaking of himself: I'm
E is ecstasy, so Es are ecstasy tablets

annotation.surface: A boss confesses the setter is tied to drug rings.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rings" looks like a noun for criminal gangs but is the verb: a bell chimes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: a church bell rings out, or chimes, the hour.

entries.clue: Rock 'n roll pioneer Bush? (5)

blocks.note: the surname of Buddy, the bespectacled 1950s Texan singer of 'Peggy Sue'
a prickly evergreen shrub with red berries, used at Christmas

annotation.surface: Asks whether some rock pioneer was called Bush, like Kate Bush.
annotation.walkthrough: Buddy HOLLY was a rock 'n' roll pioneer. Bush reads as a surname, like Kate Bush, but is the plant.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a famous surname by example, and the Christmas shrub, which grows as a bush.

entries.clue: State of inmates on getting pissed (9)

indicatorNotes.getting pissed: pissed is British slang for drunk, so the letters stagger about

annotation.surface: Prisoners are getting drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang pissed means drunk, not angry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Minnesota is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

entries.clue: Secure each day in the pen (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' says what is in the pen: each day's letters are penned inside STY

blocks.note: a sty is a pen for pigs; first part
ea is the abbreviation for each
d is the abbreviation for day

annotation.surface: Something is kept locked in a pen every day.
annotation.walkthrough: The pen is not for writing but a pigsty.
annotation.definitionFit: Secure and steady both mean firmly fixed.

entries.clue: Herb's an old crown loyalist, one turned republican (7)

indicatorNotes.turned: to turn republican is to change sides, so the one changes into a republican, I becoming R

blocks.note: Ian Paisley, the late Northern Ireland unionist leader

annotation.surface: A man named Herb was once a staunch royalist but became a republican.
annotation.walkthrough: Ian Paisley led Ulster's loyalists, loyal to the British crown; turning his one into a republican is a political joke as well as a letter swap.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: parsley is the commonest kitchen herb, the green garnish.

entries.clue: Roman ice houses – hysterical! (5)

indicatorNotes.houses: the words hold the answer inside them

annotation.surface: Italian ice-cream parlours are a riot.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Manic and hysterical both mean wildly overexcited.

entries.clue: Labour leader eagerly starts wearing shift for a dare (9)

indicatorNotes.starts: take the starts of Labour, leader and eagerly
indicatorNotes.wearing: CHANGE wears them, so they go inside it

annotation.surface: The Labour leader eagerly puts on a work shift as a bet.
annotation.walkthrough: "Labour leader" wants to be Starmer, but it is just two more words whose first letters are taken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doing something for a dare means taking up someone's provocation to prove your nerve.

entries.clue: Those who oppose any moves against speakers (9)

indicatorNotes.moves: the letters of ANY move about
indicatorNotes.against: against means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

annotation.surface: Opponents of any motion against people giving speeches.
annotation.walkthrough: "Moves" suggests Commons motions, but it rearranges ANY.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: those who say 'nay', no, to every proposal.

entries.clue: Lammy's latest lie about Department's return (5)

indicatorNotes.latest: the latest letter of Lammy is its last
indicatorNotes.about: the letters of LIE are moved about

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for department

annotation.surface: David Lammy's newest lie concerns his ministry's comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: David Lammy is a senior Labour minister. "Return" is the financial sense: the yield on an investment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the financial sense: the income an investment pays back, as in a bond's percentage.

entries.clue: Pun about helper working as a volunteer? (6)

indicatorNotes.about: the letters of PUN are turned about

annotation.surface: A joke about an assistant doing voluntary work.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: volunteers work unpaid.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: volunteering means giving your labour without wages, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Arrogance of Post Office managerial head so perverse in sorrow (9)

indicatorNotes.head: the head of managerial is its first letter
indicatorNotes.perverse: perverse means contrary, so the letters of SO turn wrong way
indicatorNotes.in: 'in sorrow' places the jumbled letters within the word for sorrow

blocks.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office

annotation.surface: Post Office bosses' high-handedness, so shameful given the grief caused.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Post Office Horizon scandal, where hundreds of UK sub-postmasters were wrongly prosecuted.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: both name an inflated sense of one's own importance.

entries.clue: Penis somehow working, for which granddad is grateful? (7)

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters are rearranged in some way

blocks.note: on = working, as a machine is on

annotation.surface: A grandfather is thankful his manhood still functions.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a smutty joke about an old man's virility; the definition is really his retirement income.
annotation.definitionFit: A pension is what a retired grandfather is grateful to receive.

entries.clue: Description of tropical island that gets tabloid smacked (3-6)

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a smacker is slang for a kiss

annotation.surface: An island paradise ends up slammed by the gutter press.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun is a UK tabloid newspaper, and a smacker is a loud kiss, so smacked here means kissed, not hit.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: travel brochures use the word for any warm, sunny beach destination.

entries.clue: Orbiter leader dropped drug (7)

annotation.surface: A spacecraft's commander let go of some medication.
annotation.walkthrough: "Orbiter" suggests a spacecraft, but it is an asteroid.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: steroids are the drugs used in medicine and, illicitly, by bodybuilders.

entries.clue: Reassuring signal – nothing dirty! (3,5)

blocks.note: the signal that danger has passed

annotation.surface: A signal that all is clean and safe.
annotation.walkthrough: The all-clear is the siren that ends an air raid; read literally, all clear means nothing is murky.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the siren sounded when an air raid ended, and a literal reading that everything is clean.

entries.clue: Cyclops's sex with fed – "Ape!" (7)

indicatorNotes.with: the pieces go together in order

annotation.surface: The setter's sex with a federal agent, and a shout of "Ape!"
annotation.walkthrough: Fed looks like an FBI agent but is simply ate. Ape is the verb, to copy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: apes are famed mimics, so to ape is to copy.

entries.clue: Biden finally steps into local mess: "Always ready to do duty" (2,4)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the end letter of Biden is used
indicatorNotes.steps into: to step into something is to join it, so that letter joins the word that follows
indicatorNotes.mess: the letters are made a mess of

annotation.surface: Joe Biden wades into some neighbourhood muddle, saying he's always ready to serve.
annotation.walkthrough: N joins LOCAL, and all six letters are jumbled together.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone on call is ready to work whenever needed.

entries.clue: Son, wallowing in hock, gets a cab (6)

indicatorNotes.wallowing: wallowing means rolling about, so the letters of SON roll
indicatorNotes.in: the jumbled letters go inside HAM

blocks.note: ham = hock, the leg joint of a pig; first part

annotation.surface: A son, drowning in debt from pawning things, hails a taxi.
annotation.walkthrough: "In hock" wants to mean in debt or pawned; here hock is the joint of meat.
annotation.definitionFit: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab.

entries.clue: Political commentator traps disheartened Conservative who got stoned? (6)

indicatorNotes.traps: to trap something is to hold it captive, so the commentator's name closes round the other letters
indicatorNotes.disheartened: Tory loses its heart, the middle letters

blocks.note: Andrew Marr, BBC political journalist; first part

annotation.surface: A pundit corners a demoralised Tory who was high on drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: Stoned suggests drugs, but it is Saint Stephen, the first Christian martyr, stoned to death.
annotation.definitionFit: Saint Stephen, stoned to death, is the classic martyr.
annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a clause for 'one who got stoned', standing for the noun.

entries.clue: In the middle of one, Gnome all but flips (5)

indicatorNotes.all but: all but means nearly all, so the word loses one letter, its last

annotation.surface: Private Eye's Lord Gnome turns somersaults.
annotation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's fictional proprietor.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the preposition: to stand among a crowd is to be surrounded by it.

entries.clue: House before Yvette's last clanger (5)

indicatorNotes.before: GAFF comes before the next piece
indicatorNotes.last: the last of a word is its end letter, so only Yvette's final letter is taken

blocks.note: gaff is British slang for a house or home

annotation.surface: The Commons ahead of Yvette Cooper's latest blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: House suggests the Commons, but a gaff is British slang for a home. Yvette Cooper is a Labour minister. A clanger is a blunder.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: to drop a clanger is to make an embarrassing blunder.

entries.clue: Hard-headed Republican elicits a reaction (9)

indicatorNotes.reaction: re-action: the letters are put into action again, in a new order

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican

annotation.surface: A tough-minded Republican provokes a response.
annotation.walkthrough: Reaction looks like the response being provoked, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hard-headed person is unsentimental and sees things as they are.

entries.clue: Plot to upend vehicle in races (5)

indicatorNotes.upend: in a down clue, upending turns the word bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the upended word goes in TT

blocks.note: the TT races on the Isle of Man; first T

annotation.surface: A scheme to flip a car during a race.
annotation.walkthrough: Plot looks like a scheme but is a piece of land. The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the land sense: an area of ground, though a tract is usually larger than a plot.

entries.clue: Second family, fine material for Scrooge (9)

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
f is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

annotation.surface: A man's second family gets good cloth from a miser.
annotation.walkthrough: Scrooge, from Dickens's A Christmas Carol, stands for any miser.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Dickens's miser Ebenezer Scrooge has become a byword for any tight-fisted person.

entries.clue: see 2dn.
Ex-PM's on edge – chaos! (6)

indicatorNotes.on: MAY is on, next to, the next piece

blocks.note: Theresa May, former UK prime minister
a hem is the edge of cloth

annotation.surface: A former prime minister is nervous, and it's pandemonium.
annotation.walkthrough: Theresa May was UK prime minister 2016-19. On edge looks like nervous; edge is the hem of a garment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: mayhem is violent disorder, total confusion.

entries.clue: Tear drop shed for Al-Fayed type? (8)

indicatorNotes.shed: the letters are shed and scattered

annotation.surface: Crying over the late Harrods owner.
annotation.walkthrough: Mohamed Al-Fayed, the late Harrods owner, was accused after his death of sexual abuse by many women.
annotation.definitionFit: Al-Fayed has been widely described as a sexual predator.
